docs.title: Configuration Overview
docs.text: m9m can be configured through configuration files, environment variables, and command-line flags.

docs.title: Configuration Methods
docs.text: Method Priority Use Case Command-line flags Highest Quick overrides Environment variables Medium Container deployments Configuration file Lowest Persistent settings

docs.title: Configuration File Location
docs.text:
m9m looks for configuration in these locations (in order):

  1. ./config.yaml (current directory)
  2. ~/.m9m/config/config.yaml (user directory)
  3. /etc/m9m/config.yaml (system-wide)

docs.title: Quick Start Configuration
docs.text:
Minimal configuration to get started:

# config.yaml
server:
host: "0.0.0.0"
port: 8080
database:
type: "sqlite"
sqlite:
path: "./data/m9m.db"
queue:
type: "sqlite"
sqlite:
path: "./data/queue.db"

docs.title: Configuration Sections
docs.text: Section Description Server Host, port, TLS settings Database Storage backend configuration Queue Job queue settings Security Authentication, CORS Environment Environment variables

docs.title: Full Configuration Example
docs.text:
# Server
server:
host: "0.0.0.0"
port: 8080
tls:
enabled: false
# Database
database:
type: "sqlite"
sqlite:
path: "./data/m9m.db"
# Queue
queue:
type: "sqlite"
max_workers: 4
sqlite:
path: "./data/queue.db"
# Logging
logging:
level: "info"
format: "json"
# Security
security:
jwt:
enabled: true
secret: "your-secret-key"
expiration: "24h"
cors:
enabled: true
allowed_origins:
- "http://localhost:3000"
# Execution
execution:
timeout: "1h"
retry:
enabled: true
max_attempts: 3

docs.title: Validating Configuration
docs.text:
Check your configuration:

m9m config validate

View effective configuration:

m9m config show

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Server Configuration
  • Database Configuration
  • Security Configuration

docs.title: Database Configuration
docs.text: Configure the storage backend for workflows, executions, and credentials.

docs.title: Supported Backends
docs.text: Backend Use Case SQLite Development, single-node PostgreSQL Production, multi-node

docs.title: SQLite (Default)
docs.text:
Zero-dependency local storage:

database:
type: "sqlite"
sqlite:
path: "./data/m9m.db"
Setting Default Description sqlite.path ~/.m9m/data/m9m.db Database file path

docs.title: CLI Override
docs.text: m9m serve --db /custom/path/m9m.db

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text:
• No external dependencies
  • Simple backup (copy file)
  • Good for development
  • Sufficient for single-node production

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Single writer (no concurrent writes)
  • Not suitable for clustered deployments

docs.title: PostgreSQL
docs.text:
Production-grade relational database:

database:
type: "postgres"
postgres:
host: "localhost"
port: 5432
database: "m9m"
user: "m9m"
password: "changeme"
ssl_mode: "disable"
max_connections: 25
max_idle_connections: 5
connection_lifetime: "5m"

docs.title: Connection URL
docs.text:
Alternatively, use a connection URL:

database:
type: "postgres"
postgres:
url: "postgres://user:password@localhost:5432/m9m?sslmode=require"

docs.title: CLI Override
docs.text: m9m serve --postgres "postgres://user:pass@localhost:5432/m9m"

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Setting Default Description host localhost Database host port 5432 Database port database m9m Database name user m9m Username password - Password ssl_mode disable SSL mode max_connections 25 Max open connections max_idle_connections 5 Max idle connections connection_lifetime 5m Connection max lifetime

docs.title: SSL Modes
docs.text: Mode Description disable No SSL require SSL required, no verification verify-ca Verify server certificate verify-full Verify certificate and hostname

docs.title: Create Database
docs.text:
CREATE DATABASE m9m;
CREATE USER m9m WITH PASSWORD 'your-password';
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE m9m TO m9m;

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
# SQLite
export M9M_DB_TYPE=sqlite
export M9M_DB_PATH=./data/m9m.db

# PostgreSQL
export M9M_DB_TYPE=postgres
export M9M_POSTGRES_HOST=localhost
export M9M_POSTGRES_PORT=5432
export M9M_POSTGRES_DATABASE=m9m
export M9M_POSTGRES_USER=m9m
export M9M_POSTGRES_PASSWORD=secret

docs.title: Schema Management
docs.text:
m9m automatically manages database schema:

  • Creates tables on first run
  • Runs migrations on upgrade
  • No manual schema management needed

docs.title: SQLite Backup
docs.text:
# Stop server first for consistent backup
cp ~/.m9m/data/m9m.db backup.db

# Or use SQLite backup
sqlite3 ~/.m9m/data/m9m.db ".backup backup.db"

docs.title: PostgreSQL Backup
docs.text:
pg_dump -U m9m -d m9m > backup.sql

# Restore
psql -U m9m -d m9m < backup.sql

docs.title: Data Stored
docs.text:
The database stores:

Table Contents workflows Workflow definitions executions Execution history and data credentials Encrypted credentials schedules Scheduled workflow configs settings Application settings

docs.title: PostgreSQL
docs.text:
database:
postgres:
max_connections: 50
max_idle_connections: 10
connection_lifetime: "1h"

docs.title: Connection Pooling
docs.text:
For high-traffic deployments, use PgBouncer:

database:
postgres:
url: "postgres://user:pass@pgbouncer:6432/m9m"

docs.title: Connection Refused
docs.text:
Error: connection refused

Check PostgreSQL is running and accessible:

psql -h localhost -U m9m -d m9m

docs.title: Permission Denied
docs.text:
Error: permission denied

Grant necessary permissions:

GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO m9m;
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON ALL SEQUENCES IN SCHEMA public TO m9m;

docs.title: Database Locked (SQLite)
docs.text:
Error: database is locked

Only one m9m instance can write to SQLite. Use PostgreSQL for multiple instances.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: All configuration options can be set via environment variables.

docs.title: Naming Convention
docs.text:
Environment variables use the M9M_ prefix with underscores:

config.yaml path → Environment variable
server.port     → M9M_SERVER_PORT
database.type   → M9M_DATABASE_TYPE

docs.title: Server
docs.text: Variable Default Description M9M_HOST 0.0.0.0 Server bind address M9M_PORT 8080 Server port M9M_DEV_MODE false Enable development mode

docs.title: Database
docs.text: Variable Default Description M9M_DB_TYPE sqlite Database type M9M_DB_PATH ~/.m9m/data/m9m.db SQLite path M9M_POSTGRES_URL - PostgreSQL connection URL M9M_POSTGRES_HOST localhost PostgreSQL host M9M_POSTGRES_PORT 5432 PostgreSQL port M9M_POSTGRES_DATABASE m9m PostgreSQL database M9M_POSTGRES_USER m9m PostgreSQL user M9M_POSTGRES_PASSWORD - PostgreSQL password

docs.title: Queue
docs.text: Variable Default Description M9M_QUEUE_TYPE sqlite Queue type M9M_QUEUE_PATH ~/.m9m/data/queue.db Queue SQLite path M9M_MAX_WORKERS 4 Worker threads

docs.title: Security
docs.text: Variable Default Description M9M_JWT_SECRET - JWT signing secret M9M_JWT_EXPIRATION 24h JWT expiration M9M_ENCRYPTION_KEY - Credential encryption key

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: Variable Default Description M9M_LOG_LEVEL info Log level M9M_LOG_FORMAT json Log format (json, text)

docs.title: Monitoring
docs.text: Variable Default Description M9M_METRICS_PORT 0 Metrics port (0=disabled)

docs.title: n8n Compatibility Variables
docs.text:
For compatibility with existing n8n configurations:

Variable Maps To N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY M9M_ENCRYPTION_KEY N8N_PORT M9M_PORT N8N_HOST M9M_HOST

docs.title: Basic Setup
docs.text:
export M9M_PORT=3000
export M9M_LOG_LEVEL=debug

m9m serve

docs.title: Production Setup
docs.text:
export M9M_PORT=8080
export M9M_DB_TYPE=postgres
export M9M_POSTGRES_URL="postgres://user:pass@db:5432/m9m?sslmode=require"
export M9M_QUEUE_TYPE=sqlite
export M9M_MAX_WORKERS=8
export M9M_JWT_SECRET="$(openssl rand -base64 32)"
export M9M_ENCRYPTION_KEY="$(openssl rand -base64 32)"
export M9M_LOG_LEVEL=info

m9m serve

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
# Dockerfile
ENV M9M_PORT=8080
ENV M9M_DB_TYPE=sqlite
ENV M9M_DB_PATH=/data/m9m.db

# docker-compose.yml
services:
m9m:
image: ghcr.io/maharsolution/m9m:latest
environment:
M9M_PORT: 8080
M9M_DB_TYPE: postgres
M9M_POSTGRES_URL: postgres://user:pass@db:5432/m9m
M9M_JWT_SECRET: ${JWT_SECRET}
M9M_ENCRYPTION_KEY: ${ENCRYPTION_KEY}

docs.title: Kubernetes
docs.text:
# ConfigMap for non-sensitive values
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
name: m9m-config
data:
M9M_PORT: "8080"
M9M_DB_TYPE: "postgres"
M9M_LOG_LEVEL: "info"
M9M_MAX_WORKERS: "8"

# Secret for sensitive values
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
name: m9m-secrets
type: Opaque
stringData:
M9M_JWT_SECRET: "your-jwt-secret"
M9M_ENCRYPTION_KEY: "your-encryption-key"
M9M_POSTGRES_URL: "postgres://..."

# Deployment
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
spec:
template:
spec:
containers:
- name: m9m
envFrom:
- configMapRef:
name: m9m-config
- secretRef:
name: m9m-secrets

docs.title: .env File
docs.text:
Create a .env file in your project:

# .env
M9M_PORT=8080
M9M_DB_TYPE=sqlite
M9M_LOG_LEVEL=debug
M9M_JWT_SECRET=development-secret-key-32-chars-min
M9M_ENCRYPTION_KEY=development-encryption-key-32chars

Load with:

source .env
m9m serve

# Or with direnv
# .envrc
dotenv

docs.title: Priority Order
docs.text:
Configuration is applied in this order (later overrides earlier):

  1. Default values
  2. Configuration file (config.yaml)
  3. Environment variables
  4. Command-line flags

Example:

# config.yaml has port: 8080
# Environment has M9M_PORT=3000
# CLI has --port 4000
# Result: port 4000 is used

docs.title: Viewing Configuration
docs.text:
See effective configuration:

m9m config show

Check a specific variable:

m9m config get database.type

docs.title: Variable Not Applied
docs.text:
• Check spelling and prefix (M9M_)
  • Verify export: echo $M9M_PORT
  • Check override order (CLI > env > file)

docs.title: Secret in Logs
docs.text:
• Use M9M_LOG_LEVEL=info (not debug)
  • Sensitive values are redacted in logs

docs.title: AI assistant
docs.text:
The in-app AI assistant (formerly "Copilot") reads M9M_AI_* env vars at boot. Any value set here can be overridden at runtime through Settings → AI or PUT /api/v1/ai.

Variable Default Description M9M_AI_ENABLED false Master on/off for the AI assistant M9M_AI_PROVIDER openai openai, anthropic, minimax, ollama M9M_AI_MODEL provider-specific Model name (e.g. gpt-4o, claude-3-5-sonnet-latest, MiniMax-Plus) M9M_AI_API_KEY — Provider API key M9M_AI_BASE_URL provider-specific Override the default API endpoint

Example — Anthropic:

export M9M_AI_ENABLED=true
export M9M_AI_PROVIDER=anthropic
export M9M_AI_MODEL=claude-3-5-sonnet-latest
export M9M_AI_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
m9m serve

Example — MiniMax (OpenAI-compatible):

export M9M_AI_ENABLED=true
export M9M_AI_PROVIDER=minimax
export M9M_AI_MODEL=MiniMax-Plus
export M9M_AI_API_KEY=...
export M9M_AI_BASE_URL=https://api.minimax.chat/v1
m9m serve

docs.title: Legacy aliases (deprecated)
docs.text:
The legacy M9M_COPILOT_* env vars remain honoured as aliases of M9M_AI_*:

Legacy Current M9M_COPILOT_ENABLED M9M_AI_ENABLED M9M_COPILOT_PROVIDER M9M_AI_PROVIDER M9M_COPILOT_MODEL M9M_AI_MODEL M9M_COPILOT_API_KEY M9M_AI_API_KEY M9M_COPILOT_BASE_URL M9M_AI_BASE_URL

These will be removed in a future major release. Migrate to the M9M_AI_* names.

docs.title: Telemetry
docs.text:
OpenTelemetry tracing configuration. Mirrors OTEL_SDK_* from the upstream SDK with m9m-specific overrides.

Variable Default Description M9M_OTEL_ENABLED false Master on/off M9M_OTEL_PROTOCOL grpc grpc or http M9M_OTEL_ENDPOINT localhost:4317 OTLP endpoint (host:port for gRPC, full URL for HTTP) M9M_OTEL_HEADERS — Comma-separated key=value pairs (e.g. x-api-key=abc,foo=bar) M9M_OTEL_SAMPLE_RATIO 1.0 (when enabled) 0.0–1.0

If both M9M_OTEL_* and the standard OTEL_SDK_* variables are set, M9M_OTEL_* wins.

A DB-stored override layer (set via PUT /api/v1/otel) wins over env. See Observability and Telemetry API.

docs.title: Sync service (n8n ↔ m9m)
docs.text:
The bundled sync-service/sync.py reads these env vars. They are usually set in docker-compose.yml, not the host shell.

Variable Default Description N8N_BASE_URL http://n8n-designer-frontend:5678 n8n REST API base URL N8N_API_KEY — n8n API key M9M_BASE_URL http://m9m-backend:8080 m9m REST API base URL POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS 30 Background poll cadence SYNC_ONLY_ACTIVE true Only push active: true workflows SYNC_PORT 8001 Bridge's HTTP API listen port N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY — n8n's encryption key (also reads GEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY) N8N_PG_HOST postgres-db n8n Postgres host N8N_PG_PORT 5432 n8n Postgres port N8N_PG_USER database_admin n8n Postgres user N8N_PG_PASSWORD Secure_Db_Pass_2026 n8n Postgres password (change in production) N8N_PG_DATABASE n8n_prod n8n Postgres database

Full reference: n8n ↔ m9m sync bridge.

docs.title: Queue Configuration
docs.text: Configure the job queue for workflow execution.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The job queue manages asynchronous workflow executions. When you execute a workflow asynchronously, a job is created, queued, and processed by worker threads.

docs.title: Supported Queue Types
docs.text: Type Persistence Use Case memory No Development, testing sqlite Yes Production (single-node)

docs.title: SQLite Queue (Default)
docs.text:
Persistent queue with SQLite storage:

queue:
type: "sqlite"
max_workers: 4
sqlite:
path: "./data/queue.db"
Setting Default Description sqlite.path ~/.m9m/data/queue.db Queue database path

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text:
• Jobs survive server restarts
  • No external dependencies
  • Recovery of failed jobs

docs.title: CLI Override
docs.text: m9m serve --queue sqlite --queue-db /data/queue.db

docs.title: Memory Queue
docs.text:
Fast in-memory queue (jobs lost on restart):

queue:
type: "memory"
max_workers: 4

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text:
• Fastest performance
  • No disk I/O

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Jobs lost on restart
  • Not suitable for production

docs.title: CLI Override
docs.text: m9m serve --queue memory

docs.title: Worker Configuration
docs.text:
queue:
max_workers: 10
Setting Default Description max_workers 4 Concurrent workflow executions

docs.title: CLI Override
docs.text: m9m serve --workers 8

docs.title: Worker Sizing
docs.text: Scenario Workers Development 2-4 Light production 4-8 Heavy production 8-16 CPU-bound workflows Match CPU cores I/O-bound workflows 2-4x CPU cores

docs.title: Job Retry Configuration
docs.text:
execution:
retry:
enabled: true
max_attempts: 3
backoff: "exponential"
initial_interval: "1s"
max_interval: "5m"
Setting Default Description enabled true Enable automatic retry max_attempts 3 Maximum retry attempts backoff exponential Backoff strategy initial_interval 1s First retry delay max_interval 5m Maximum retry delay

docs.title: Backoff Strategies
docs.text: Strategy Behavior linear Constant delay between retries exponential Doubling delay (1s, 2s, 4s, ...)

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
export M9M_QUEUE_TYPE=sqlite
export M9M_QUEUE_PATH=./data/queue.db
export M9M_MAX_WORKERS=8

docs.title: Job Lifecycle
docs.text:
Enqueue → Pending → Running → Completed
                      ↓
                    Failed → Retry → Pending (loop)
                      ↓
                    Failed (max retries)

docs.title: Queue Stats API
docs.text:
curl http://localhost:8080/api/v1/jobs/stats

Response:

{
"pending": 5,
"running": 2,
"completed": 1500,
"failed": 23,
"workers": 4,
"queueType": "sqlite"
}

docs.title: Prometheus Metrics
docs.text:
# HELP m9m_queue_pending_jobs Number of pending jobs
m9m_queue_pending_jobs 5

# HELP m9m_queue_running_jobs Number of running jobs
m9m_queue_running_jobs 2

# HELP m9m_queue_workers Number of active workers
m9m_queue_workers 4

docs.title: SQLite Queue Recovery
docs.text:
On server restart, the SQLite queue:

  1. Loads pending jobs from database
  2. Requeues jobs that were running (may have been interrupted)
  3. Resumes processing

docs.title: Manual Recovery
docs.text:
View stuck jobs:

curl "http://localhost:8080/api/v1/jobs?status=running"

docs.title: Production Setup
docs.text:
queue:
type: "sqlite"
max_workers: 8
sqlite:
path: "/data/queue.db"
execution:
retry:
enabled: true
max_attempts: 3
backoff: "exponential"

docs.title: High Throughput
docs.text:
queue:
type: "sqlite"
max_workers: 16

docs.title: Resource Constrained
docs.text:
queue:
type: "sqlite"
max_workers: 2

docs.title: Jobs Not Processing
docs.text:
Check workers are running:

curl http://localhost:8080/api/v1/jobs/stats

If workers: 0, restart the server.

docs.title: Jobs Stuck in Pending
docs.text:
Check for errors in logs:

tail -f ~/.m9m/logs/m9m.log | grep -i queue

docs.title: Queue Database Corruption
docs.text:
Recreate queue database:

# Stop server
rm ~/.m9m/data/queue.db
# Start server (recreates database)
m9m serve

Note: This loses pending jobs.

docs.title: Security Configuration
docs.text: Configure authentication, authorization, and security settings.

docs.title: JWT Authentication
docs.text:
security:
jwt:
enabled: true
secret: "your-secret-key-minimum-32-characters"
expiration: "24h"
Setting Default Description enabled true Enable JWT auth secret - Signing secret (min 32 chars) expiration 24h Token lifetime

Secret Key

Use a strong, random secret. Generate one with: 

openssl rand -base64 32

docs.title: API Keys
docs.text:
security:
api_keys:
enabled: true

API keys provide programmatic access without JWT tokens.

docs.title: Basic Authentication
docs.text:
security:
basic_auth:
enabled: false
username: "admin"
password: "changeme"

Use Sparingly

Basic auth is best for development or when behind a secure reverse proxy.

docs.title: CORS Configuration
docs.text:
security:
cors:
enabled: true
allowed_origins:
- "https://app.example.com"
- "http://localhost:3000"
allowed_methods:
- "GET"
- "POST"
- "PUT"
- "DELETE"
- "PATCH"
allowed_headers:
- "Content-Type"
- "Authorization"
- "X-API-Key"
allow_credentials: true
max_age: 86400
Setting Description allowed_origins Origins allowed to access API allowed_methods HTTP methods allowed allowed_headers Headers allowed in requests allow_credentials Allow cookies/auth headers max_age Preflight cache duration (seconds)

docs.title: Development Mode
docs.text:
In dev mode, CORS is permissive:

m9m serve --dev

Equivalent to:

security:
cors:
allowed_origins: ["*"]

docs.title: Credential Encryption
docs.text:
credentials:
encryption_key: "your-encryption-key-minimum-32-characters"
storage: "database"
Setting Description encryption_key AES-256 encryption key storage Where to store credentials

Encryption Key

  • Keep this key secret and backed up
  • Changing the key makes existing credentials unreadable
  • Generate with: openssl rand -base64 32

docs.title: Rate Limiting
docs.text:
performance:
rate_limit:
enabled: true
requests_per_minute: 60
burst: 10
Setting Default Description enabled false Enable rate limiting requests_per_minute 60 Requests per minute per IP burst 10 Burst allowance

docs.title: TLS/HTTPS
docs.text:
server:
tls:
enabled: true
cert_file: "/path/to/cert.pem"
key_file: "/path/to/key.pem"

See Server Configuration for details.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
# JWT
export M9M_JWT_SECRET=your-secret-key
export M9M_JWT_EXPIRATION=24h

# Credentials
export M9M_ENCRYPTION_KEY=your-encryption-key

# Also supports n8n-style for compatibility
export N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY=your-encryption-key

docs.title: Security Headers
docs.text:
m9m sets security headers automatically:

Header Value X-Content-Type-Options nosniff X-Frame-Options DENY X-XSS-Protection 1; mode=block

docs.title: Production Configuration
docs.text:
security:
jwt:
enabled: true
secret: "${JWT_SECRET}"  # From environment
expiration: "8h"
api_keys:
enabled: true
cors:
enabled: true
allowed_origins:
- "https://your-app.com"
allow_credentials: true
credentials:
encryption_key: "${ENCRYPTION_KEY}"  # From environment
server:
tls:
enabled: true
cert_file: "/etc/ssl/certs/m9m.pem"
key_file: "/etc/ssl/private/m9m.key"
performance:
rate_limit:
enabled: true
requests_per_minute: 100

docs.title: Secret Management
docs.text:
Store secrets in environment variables:

export JWT_SECRET=$(cat /run/secrets/jwt_secret)
export ENCRYPTION_KEY=$(cat /run/secrets/encryption_key)

Or use a secret manager (Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, etc.).

docs.title: Network Security
docs.text:
• Run behind a reverse proxy (nginx, traefik)
  • Use TLS for all connections
  • Restrict network access to trusted IPs
  • Use firewall rules

docs.title: Regular Audits
docs.text:
• Rotate JWT secrets periodically
  • Revoke unused API keys
  • Review access logs
  • Update to latest versions

docs.title: Invalid Token
docs.text:
Error: invalid or expired token
  • Check JWT secret matches
  • Check token hasn't expired
  • Regenerate token

docs.title: CORS Errors
docs.text:
Access-Control-Allow-Origin missing
  • Add origin to allowed_origins
  • Check for trailing slashes in URLs
  • Verify allow_credentials if using auth

docs.title: Encryption Errors
docs.text:
Error: cipher: message authentication failed
  • Encryption key doesn't match
  • Credential data corrupted
  • Key must be exactly 32 characters

docs.title: Server Configuration

docs.title: Basic Settings
docs.text:

host: "0.0.0.0"
port: 8080

docs.title: TLS/HTTPS
docs.text:
Enable HTTPS with TLS certificates:

server:
host: "0.0.0.0"
port: 443
tls:
enabled: true
cert_file: "/path/to/cert.pem"
key_file: "/path/to/key.pem"
Setting Description tls.enabled Enable HTTPS tls.cert_file Path to certificate file tls.key_file Path to private key file

docs.title: Generate Self-Signed Certificate
docs.text:
For development:

openssl req -x509 -nodes -days 365 -newkey rsa:2048 \
-keyout key.pem -out cert.pem \
-subj "/CN=localhost"

docs.title: Timeouts
docs.text:
server:
read_timeout: "30s"
write_timeout: "60s"
idle_timeout: "120s"
Setting Default Description read_timeout 30s Max time to read request write_timeout 60s Max time to write response idle_timeout 120s Keep-alive timeout

docs.title: Command-Line Flags
docs.text:
Override via CLI:

m9m serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 3000
Flag Config Equivalent --host server.host --port server.port

docs.text:
export M9M_HOST=0.0.0.0

docs.text:
Enable development mode for permissive CORS:

m9m serve --dev

Or in configuration:

development:
debug: true

docs.title: Bind Address Examples
docs.text: Address Description 0.0.0.0 All interfaces (default) 127.0.0.1 Localhost only 192.168.1.100 Specific interface :: All IPv6 interfaces

docs.title: Behind a Reverse Proxy
docs.text:
When running behind nginx/traefik:

server:
host: "127.0.0.1"
port: 8080
# Trust X-Forwarded-* headers
trusted_proxies:
- "127.0.0.1"
- "10.0.0.0/8"

docs.title: Nginx Configuration
docs.text:
server {
listen 443 ssl;
server_name m9m.example.com;
ssl_certificate /path/to/cert.pem;
ssl_certificate_key /path/to/key.pem;
location / {
proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080;
proxy_set_header Host $host;
proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
}
# WebSocket support
location /push {
proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080;
proxy_http_version 1.1;
proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";
}
}

docs.title: Credentials Overview
docs.text: Securely store and manage authentication credentials for nodes.

docs.title: What are Credentials?
docs.text:
Credentials store sensitive authentication data:

  • API keys
  • OAuth tokens
  • Database passwords
  • Service account keys

docs.title: Security Features
docs.text: Feature Description AES-256 encryption Credentials encrypted at rest Access control Per-workflow credential access Audit logging Track credential usage Secure storage Never exposed in logs or API

docs.title: Credential Structure
docs.text:
{
"id": "cred-123",
"name": "My API Key",
"type": "apiKey",
"data": {
"apiKey": "encrypted..."
},
"createdAt": "2024-01-15T10:00:00Z",
"updatedAt": "2024-01-15T10:00:00Z"
}

docs.title: Via CLI
docs.text: m9m credential create --name "GitHub Token" --type oauth2 --data @creds.json

docs.title: Via API
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/credentials \
-H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{
    "name": "My API Key",
    "type": "apiKey",
    "data": {
      "apiKey": "sk-xxx..."
    }
  }'

docs.title: In Workflow JSON
docs.text:
Reference credentials by ID or name:

{
"nodes": [
{
"type": "n8n-nodes-base.httpRequest",
"parameters": {
"authentication": "genericCredentialType",
"genericAuthType": "httpHeaderAuth"
},
"credentials": {
"httpHeaderAuth": {
"id": "cred-123",
"name": "My API Key"
}
}
}
]
}

docs.title: In Expressions
docs.text:
Access credential data:

{{ $credentials.apiKey }}

docs.title: List Credentials
docs.text: m9m credential list

docs.title: Get Credential
docs.text: m9m credential get cred-123

docs.title: Update Credential
docs.text: m9m credential update cred-123 --data @new-creds.json

docs.title: Delete Credential
docs.text: m9m credential delete cred-123

docs.title: 1. Use Descriptive Names
docs.text:
Good: "Production GitHub - CI/CD"
Bad:  "github1"

docs.title: 2. Rotate Regularly
docs.text:
• Set up credential rotation schedules
  • Update workflows after rotation
  • Monitor for failures after rotation

docs.title: 3. Limit Scope
docs.text:
• Grant minimal permissions
  • Use separate credentials per environment
  • Avoid shared credentials across workflows

docs.title: 4. Audit Access
docs.text:
# View credential usage
m9m credential audit cred-123

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
For local development, use environment variables:

export API_KEY="your-key"

Access in expressions:

{{ $env.API_KEY }}

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Set encryption key:

credentials:
encryptionKey: "your-32-byte-encryption-key-here"

Or via environment:

export M9M_CREDENTIALS_ENCRYPTION_KEY="your-key"

docs.title: Key Management
docs.text:
• Use strong, random 32-byte keys
  • Store keys securely (vault, KMS)
  • Rotate keys periodically

docs.title: Credential Validation
docs.text:
Each credential type is validated on creation:

# Test credential validity
m9m credential test cred-123

Returns:

{
"valid": true,
"message": "Successfully authenticated"
}

docs.title: OAuth2 Token Refresh
docs.text:
m9m automatically refreshes expired OAuth2 tokens:

  1. Detects expired access token
  2. Uses refresh token to get new access token
  3. Updates stored credential
  4. Retries the request

docs.title: Production Checklist

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
• [ ] Set strong JWT secret 

    M9M_JWT_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 32)

  • [ ] Configure JWT expiration 

    security:
jwtExpiration: 24h
refreshTokenExpiration: 168h

  • [ ] Enable API key authentication for service accounts

docs.title: Encryption
docs.text:
• [ ] Set encryption key for credentials 

    M9M_ENCRYPTION_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16)

  • [ ] Enable TLS/HTTPS 

    server:
tls:
enabled: true
certFile: /etc/m9m/tls.crt
keyFile: /etc/m9m/tls.key

docs.title: Network
docs.text:
• [ ] Configure CORS appropriately 

    security:
cors:
allowedOrigins:
- "https://app.example.com"

- GET
- POST
- PUT

  • [ ] Set up firewall rules

rateLimit:
enabled: true
requests: 100
window: 60

docs.title: Access Control
docs.text:

enablePprof: false

  • [ ] Use minimal permissions for service accounts

maxOpenConns: 25

docs.title: Expressions Overview
docs.text: Expressions allow dynamic values in node parameters using data from previous nodes.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
Expressions use double curly braces:

{{ expression }}

docs.title: Access JSON Data
docs.text: {{ $json.fieldName }}

docs.title: String Interpolation
docs.text: Hello, {{ $json.name }}! You have {{ $json.count }} messages.

docs.title: Mathematical Operations
docs.text: {{ $json.price * $json.quantity }}

docs.title: Expression Context
docs.text:
Every expression has access to:

Variable Description $json Current item's JSON data $item Current item index (0-based) $node Access other nodes' output $input Input data helpers $env Environment variables $now Current timestamp

docs.title: Where to Use Expressions
docs.text:
Expressions work in most node parameter fields:

{
"type": "n8n-nodes-base.httpRequest",
"parameters": {
"url": "https://api.example.com/users/{{ $json.userId }}",
"method": "GET"
}
}

docs.title: Simple Reference
docs.text:
Direct field access:

{{ $json.email }}

docs.title: Nested Access
docs.text:
Access nested objects:

{{ $json.user.address.city }}

docs.title: Array Access
docs.text:
Access array elements:

{{ $json.items[0].name }}

docs.title: Conditional
docs.text:
Ternary expressions:

{{ $json.status === "active" ? "Yes" : "No" }}

docs.title: Function Calls
docs.text:
Use built-in functions:

{{ $json.name.toUpperCase() }}

docs.title: Data Flow Example
docs.text:
Node A outputs: { "user": "John", "score": 85 }
     ↓
Node B receives and uses: {{ $json.user }} scored {{ $json.score }}
     ↓
Result: "John scored 85"

docs.title: Undefined Values
docs.text:
Use optional chaining:

{{ $json.user?.name ?? "Unknown" }}

docs.title: Default Values
docs.text:
Provide fallbacks:

{{ $json.count || 0 }}

docs.title: Code Node
docs.text:
Test expressions in a Code node:

return items.map(item => ({
json: {
original: item.json,
computed: item.json.value * 2
}
}));

docs.title: Log Output
docs.text:
Log values for debugging:

console.log($json);
return items;

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Use meaningful field names - Makes expressions readable
  2. Handle missing data - Use defaults and null checks
  3. Keep expressions simple - Complex logic belongs in Code nodes
  4. Test with sample data - Verify before production

docs.text:
The current item's JSON data:

// Item: { "name": "John", "age": 30 }
{{ $json.name }}      // "John"
{{ $json.age }}       // 30
{{ $json }}           // { "name": "John", "age": 30 }

Current item index (0-based):

// Processing 3 items

Access all input data:

{{ $input.item }}             // Current input item

Access output from any node by name:

{{ $node["Node Name"].json.field }}

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: Welcome to m9m! This guide will help you get up and running quickly.

docs.title: What is m9m?
docs.text:
m9m is a high-performance workflow automation platform that provides:

  • n8n Compatibility - Run existing n8n workflows without modification
  • Superior Performance - 5-10x faster execution than n8n
  • Lower Resource Usage - 70% less memory, 75% smaller containers
  • Cloud Native - Built for modern infrastructure

docs.title: Option 1: Binary Installation
docs.text:
# Install with Go
go install github.com/maharsolution/m9m/cmd/m9m@latest

# Start the server
m9m serve

docs.title: Option 2: Docker
docs.text:
# Run with Docker
docker run -p 8080:8080 ghcr.io/maharsolution/m9m:latest

docs.title: Option 3: From Source
docs.text:
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/maharsolution/m9m.git
cd m9m

# Build
make build

# Run
./m9m serve

docs.title: Verify Installation
docs.text:
Once running, verify m9m is working:

# Check health endpoint
curl http://localhost:8080/health

# Expected response:
# {"status":"ok"}

docs.title: Access Points
docs.text:
After starting m9m, you can access:

Service URL Description Web UI http://localhost:8080 Visual workflow editor REST API http://localhost:8080/api/v1 Programmatic access Health http://localhost:8080/health Health check endpoint Metrics http://localhost:8080/metrics Prometheus metrics

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
1. Installation - Detailed installation options
  2. First Workflow - Create your first workflow
  3. Core Concepts - Understand workflows, nodes, and data flow
  4. Agent Usage Guide - Use m9m from AI agents via MCP or REST API

docs.title: Agent Usage Guide
docs.text: This guide shows how an AI agent can use m9m as an orchestration backend.

docs.title: Recommended Integration Modes
docs.text:
1. MCP mode (recommended for LLM agents)
  2. REST API mode (recommended for deterministic service-to-service control)

m9m supports both local and cloud operation: - Local: run mcp-server or m9m serve on the same machine - Cloud: point agents to a remote m9m API server

docs.title: Public Launch Notes
docs.text:
• Official launch path: single binary distribution (package manager/releases)
  • Kubernetes manifests are experimental reference material
  • Unauthenticated API exposure should be treated as internal/experimental only

docs.title: Option 1: MCP (Best For AI Assistants)
docs.text: MCP gives agents a structured tool interface (workflow, execution, debug, plugin tools).

docs.title: Start MCP Server
docs.text:
go build -o mcp-server ./cmd/mcp-server
./mcp-server --db ./data/m9m.db

docs.title: Configure Client (example)
docs.text:
{
"mcpServers": {
"m9m": {
"command": "/absolute/path/to/mcp-server",
"args": ["--db", "/absolute/path/to/data/m9m.db"]
}
}
}

docs.title: Core Agent Flow (MCP tools)
docs.text:
1. Discover capabilities: node_types_list, node_search
  2. Create or update workflows: workflow_create, workflow_update
  3. Execute: execution_run or execution_run_async
  4. Observe: execution_wait, execution_get, debug_execution_logs
  5. Recover: execution_retry or execution_cancel

docs.title: Option 2: REST API (Best For Backend Agents)
docs.text:
Base URL:

http://localhost:8080/api/v1

docs.title: 1) Discover Workflows
docs.text: curl "http://localhost:8080/api/v1/workflows?limit=20"

docs.title: 2) Execute Existing Workflow (Sync)
docs.text:
Request body supports either: - raw array: [{ "json": {...} }] - envelope: { "inputData": [{ "json": {...} }] }

curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/workflows/<workflow-id>/execute \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{"inputData":[{"json":{"task":"summarize"}}]}'

docs.title: 3) Execute Inline Workflow Definition
docs.text:
Use this when your agent composes workflows dynamically:

curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/workflows/run \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{
    "workflow": {
      "name": "Inline Run",
      "nodes": [
        {"id":"start","name":"Start","type":"n8n-nodes-base.start","parameters":{}}
      ],
      "connections": {}
    },
    "inputData": [{"json":{"requestId":"abc-123"}}]
  }'

docs.title: 4) Run Async + Poll
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/workflows/<workflow-id>/execute-async \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{"inputData":[{"json":{"batchId":"b-42"}}]}'

Then:

curl "http://localhost:8080/api/v1/jobs/<job-id>"
curl "http://localhost:8080/api/v1/executions?workflowId=<workflow-id>&limit=10"

docs.title: 5) Cancel / Retry
docs.text:
Cancel:

curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/executions/<execution-id>/cancel

Possible behavior: - 202 Accepted: cancellation requested (status: "cancel_requested") - 409 Conflict: runtime cannot cancel this execution instance

Retry failed execution:

curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/executions/<execution-id>/retry

docs.title: Practical Agent Pattern
docs.text:
Use a simple control loop:

  1. Plan: choose existing workflow or construct inline workflow
  2. Execute: run sync for short tasks, async for long tasks
  3. Observe: poll executions/jobs and inspect logs
  4. Recover: retry on transient failures, cancel when superseded
  5. Persist: save useful workflows for future reuse

docs.title: Security and Reliability Guidance
docs.text:
• Prefer authenticated API access in production
  • Use least-privilege credentials per workflow
  • For CLI agent nodes, keep sandboxEnabled=true
  • Set explicit timeouts/memory limits for long-running agent tasks
  • Track execution IDs in your agent state for robust resume/recovery

docs.title: Core Concepts
docs.text: This guide explains the fundamental concepts in m9m workflow automation.

docs.title: Workflows
docs.text:
A workflow is a directed graph of nodes that defines an automated process. Workflows consist of:

  • Nodes - Individual processing steps
  • Connections - Data flow paths between nodes
  • Settings - Workflow-level configuration

docs.title: Workflow Structure
docs.text:
{
"name": "Example Workflow",
"nodes": [...],
"connections": {...},
"settings": {...},
"active": true
}

docs.title: Workflow States
docs.text: State Description active Workflow is enabled and can be triggered inactive Workflow is disabled

docs.title: Nodes
docs.text: Nodes are the building blocks of workflows. Each node performs a specific operation.

docs.title: Node Structure
docs.text:
{
"id": "unique-id",
"name": "Display Name",
"type": "n8n-nodes-base.httpRequest",
"position": [x, y],
"parameters": {...},
"disabled": false
}

docs.title: Node Categories
docs.text: Category Description Examples Core Workflow control Start Trigger Start workflows Webhook, Cron Transform Data manipulation Set, Filter, Code HTTP Web requests HTTP Request Database Data storage PostgreSQL, MySQL Messaging Communication Slack, Discord AI AI/ML operations OpenAI, Anthropic Cloud Cloud services AWS S3, Azure Blob VCS Version control GitHub, GitLab

docs.title: Node Parameters
docs.text:
Parameters configure node behavior. They support:

  • Static values: "url": "https://api.example.com"
  • Expressions: "url": "={{ $json.endpoint }}"

docs.title: Data Items
docs.text: Data flows through workflows as items. Each item is a JSON object.

docs.title: Item Structure
docs.text:
{
"json": {
"field1": "value1",
"field2": 123
},
"binary": {
"data": "base64-encoded..."
}
}

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text:
┌─────────┐     ┌─────────┐     ┌─────────┐
│  Node A │────▶│  Node B │────▶│  Node C │
│         │     │         │     │         │
│ Output: │     │ Input:  │     │ Input:  │
│ [item1] │     │ [item1] │     │ [item2] │
│ [item2] │     │ [item2] │     │         │
└─────────┘     │ Output: │     └─────────┘
                │ [item2] │
                └─────────┘
  • Nodes receive all items from connected upstream nodes
  • Nodes can output zero, one, or many items
  • Data is passed by reference (not copied)

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: Connections define how data flows between nodes.

docs.title: Connection Structure
docs.text:
{
"Source Node Name": {
"main": [
[
{"node": "Target Node", "type": "main", "index": 0}
]
]
}
}

docs.title: Connection Types
docs.text: Type Description main Primary data flow

docs.title: Multiple Outputs
docs.text:
Some nodes have multiple outputs (e.g., Switch node):

{
"Switch": {
"main": [
[{"node": "Path A", "type": "main", "index": 0}],
[{"node": "Path B", "type": "main", "index": 0}]
]
}
}

docs.title: Expressions
docs.text: Expressions allow dynamic values based on input data.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
// Full expression
={{ $json.fieldName }}
// Template string
Hello {{ $json.name }}!
// With operations
={{ $json.price * 1.1 }}

docs.title: Available Variables
docs.text:
Variable Description $json Current item's JSON data $item Current item index $now Current timestamp $env Environment variables $input All input items

See Expressions for complete documentation.

docs.title: Executions
docs.text: An execution is a single run of a workflow.

docs.title: Execution States
docs.text: State Description pending Queued, waiting to run running Currently executing success Completed successfully failed Completed with errors cancelled Manually cancelled

docs.title: Execution Data
docs.text:
Each execution stores:

  • Input data
  • Output data from each node
  • Error messages (if failed)
  • Timing information
  • Execution mode (manual, scheduled, webhook)

docs.title: Credentials
docs.text: Credentials securely store authentication data for external services.

docs.title: Credential Structure
docs.text:
{
"name": "My API Key",
"type": "apiKey",
"data": {
"apiKey": "secret-value"
}
}

docs.title: Credential Types
docs.text:
Type Used For apiKey API key authentication oauth2 OAuth 2.0 flows basicAuth HTTP Basic Auth httpHeader Custom headers

Credentials are encrypted at rest and injected into node parameters at runtime.

docs.title: Triggers
docs.text: Triggers start workflow execution.

docs.title: Trigger Types
docs.text: Trigger Description Manual Started via API or CLI Webhook HTTP request to endpoint Schedule Cron-based timing

docs.title: Webhook Triggers
docs.text:
{
"type": "n8n-nodes-base.webhook",
"parameters": {
"path": "/my-webhook",
"httpMethod": "POST"
}
}

Endpoint: http://localhost:8080/webhook/my-webhook

docs.title: Scheduled Triggers
docs.text:
{
"type": "n8n-nodes-base.cron",
"parameters": {
"cronExpression": "0 9 * * MON"
}
}

docs.title: Job Queue
docs.text: m9m uses a job queue for workflow execution.

docs.title: Queue Behavior
docs.text:
1. Workflow execution request → Job created
  2. Job queued with status pending
  3. Worker picks up job → status running
  4. Execution completes → status success or failed

docs.title: Queue Types
docs.text: Type Persistence Use Case memory No Development, testing sqlite Yes Production (single node)

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Concept Description Workflow Directed graph of automated steps Node Single processing operation Connection Data flow path between nodes Item Unit of data (JSON object) Expression Dynamic value using input data Execution Single workflow run Credential Secure authentication storage Trigger Workflow start mechanism Queue Execution job management

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Create workflows
  • Explore nodes
  • Learn expressions

docs.title: Your first m9m workflow
docs.text: A five-minute walkthrough: fetch JSON from an API, transform the response, return the result. Then add a webhook trigger and basic error handling.

docs.title: What you'll build
docs.text:
┌─────────┐    ┌─────────────┐    ┌──────────────┐
│  Start  │───▶│ Fetch Posts │───▶│ Format Output│
└─────────┘    └─────────────┘    └──────────────┘

A workflow that:

  1. Starts via the Start node (or a webhook trigger — added later)
  2. Fetches a JSON post from jsonplaceholder.typicode.com
  3. Transforms the response into a compact summary
  4. Returns the output

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• m9m installed (installation guide)
  • curl for API calls (or the Web UI at http://localhost:8080)

docs.title: Step 1 — define the workflow
docs.text:
Save as my-first-workflow.json:

{
"name": "My First Workflow",
"nodes": [
{
"id": "start",
"name": "Start",
"type": "n8n-nodes-base.start",
"position": [250, 300],
"parameters": {}
},
{
"id": "http",
"name": "Fetch Posts",
"type": "n8n-nodes-base.httpRequest",
"position": [450, 300],
"parameters": {
"url": "https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/1",
"method": "GET"
}
},
{
"id": "set",
"name": "Format Output",
"type": "n8n-nodes-base.set",
"position": [650, 300],
"parameters": {
"assignments": [
{ "name": "title",   "value": "={{ $json.title }}" },
{ "name": "summary", "value": "Post ID: {{ $json.id }} by User {{ $json.userId }}" }
]
}
}
],
"connections": {
"Start": {
"main": [[{"node": "Fetch Posts", "type": "main", "index": 0}]]
},
"Fetch Posts": {
"main": [[{"node": "Format Output", "type": "main", "index": 0}]]
}
}
}

This is the same JSON shape n8n uses. Workflows exported from n8n drop in here.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
m9m exec my-first-workflow.json

Expected output:

{
"status": "success",
"data": [
{
"title": "sunt aut facere repellat provident occaecati excepturi optio reprehenderit",
"summary": "Post ID: 1 by User 1"
}
]
}

docs.title: REST API
docs.text:
# Create
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/workflows \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d @my-first-workflow.json

# Execute
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/workflows/{workflow-id}/execute

docs.title: Start node
docs.text:
{ "type": "n8n-nodes-base.start", "parameters": {} }

Entry point. Passes input through, or emits a single empty data item if no input is provided.

docs.title: HTTP Request node
docs.text:
{
"type": "n8n-nodes-base.httpRequest",
"parameters": {
"url": "https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/1",
"method": "GET"
}
}

Makes an HTTP call. The parsed response body is exposed to downstream nodes as $json.

docs.title: Set node
docs.text:
{
"type": "n8n-nodes-base.set",
"parameters": {
"assignments": [
{ "name": "title",   "value": "={{ $json.title }}" },
{ "name": "summary", "value": "Post ID: {{ $json.id }} by User {{ $json.userId }}" }
]
}
}

Reshapes data with expressions. Use ={{ ... }} for a value computed entirely by an expression, or interpolate inline with {{ ... }} inside a string.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
{
"Start":       { "main": [[{ "node": "Fetch Posts",  "type": "main", "index": 0 }]] },
"Fetch Posts": { "main": [[{ "node": "Format Output","type": "main", "index": 0 }]] }
}

Defines the directed graph: which node's output feeds which node's input.

docs.title: Step 4 — trigger via webhook
docs.text:
Replace the Start node with a webhook:

{
"id": "webhook",
"name": "Webhook",
"type": "n8n-nodes-base.webhook",
"position": [250, 300],
"parameters": {
"path": "/my-workflow",
"httpMethod": "POST"
}
}

Then trigger it:

curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/webhook/my-workflow \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{"custom": "data"}'

The posted body is available as $json in downstream nodes.

docs.title: Step 5 — add error handling
docs.text:
Insert a filter to short-circuit on non-2xx responses:

{
"id": "check",
"name": "Check Success",
"type": "n8n-nodes-base.filter",
"position": [550, 300],
"parameters": {
"conditions": [
{
"leftValue": "={{ $json.statusCode }}",
"operator": "equals",
"rightValue": 200
}
]
}
}

For richer error handling, see Workflow patterns › Error handling.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
1. Core Concepts — workflows, nodes, data flow, expressions
  2. Nodes Reference — all 40+ available node types
  3. Expressions — full expression syntax and built-in functions
  4. Workflow Examples — common patterns
  5. Migrate from n8n — import your existing workflows

docs.title: Install m9m
docs.text: m9m ships as a single statically-linked Go binary. Pick whichever install path fits your environment — they all produce the same binary.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Operating system: macOS, Linux, or Windows
  • Architecture: AMD64 (x86_64) or ARM64 (aarch64)
  • Disk: ~30 MB for the binary, plus storage for workflows and the job queue
  • Network: internet access for the initial download (not needed at runtime)

docs.title: Installer script (any platform) — recommended
docs.text:
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/maharsolution/m9m/main/install.sh | bash

Auto-detects OS and architecture, downloads the right binary, places it on your $PATH. Falls back to a local Go build if no prebuilt is available for your platform.

docs.title: Homebrew (macOS / Linux)
docs.text:
brew tap neul-labs/tap
brew install m9m

docs.title: Go
docs.text:
go install github.com/maharsolution/m9m/cmd/m9m@latest

Installs m9m to $GOPATH/bin. Requires Go 1.21+.

docs.title: Docker — GitHub Container Registry (releases)
docs.text:
docker run -p 8080:8080 ghcr.io/maharsolution/m9m:latest

With persistent data:

docker run -p 8080:8080 \
-v m9m-data:/app/data \
ghcr.io/maharsolution/m9m:latest

With custom configuration:

docker run -p 8080:8080 \
-v ./config.yaml:/app/config/config.yaml \
-v m9m-data:/app/data \
ghcr.io/maharsolution/m9m:latest

docs.title: Docker — Docker Hub (CI builds)
docs.text: docker run -p 8080:8080 maharsolution/m9m:latest

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
version: '3.8'
services:
m9m:
image: ghcr.io/maharsolution/m9m:latest
ports:
- "8080:8080"
volumes:
- m9m-data:/app/data
environment:
- M9M_LOG_LEVEL=info
restart: unless-stopped
volumes:
m9m-data:

docker-compose up -d

docs.title: Python SDK
docs.text:
pip install m9m-cli
# or
uv add m9m-cli
poetry add m9m-cli

The m9m-cli package downloads the binary on first use. See the PyPI page.

docs.title: Node.js SDK
docs.text:
npm install m9m-cli
# or
yarn add m9m-cli
pnpm add m9m-cli
bun add m9m-cli

The m9m-cli package downloads the binary on npm install. See the npm page.

docs.title: Build from source
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/maharsolution/m9m.git
cd m9m
make deps
make build
./m9m version

docs.title: Prebuilt binaries
docs.text:
Download directly from GitHub Releases.

Linux AMD64Linux ARM64macOS AMD64 (Intel)macOS ARM64 (Apple Silicon)Windows AMD64 
curl -LO https://github.com/maharsolution/m9m/releases/latest/download/m9m-linux-amd64
chmod +x m9m-linux-amd64
sudo mv m9m-linux-amd64 /usr/local/bin/m9m

curl -LO https://github.com/maharsolution/m9m/releases/latest/download/m9m-linux-arm64
chmod +x m9m-linux-arm64
sudo mv m9m-linux-arm64 /usr/local/bin/m9m

curl -LO https://github.com/maharsolution/m9m/releases/latest/download/m9m-darwin-amd64
chmod +x m9m-darwin-amd64
sudo mv m9m-darwin-amd64 /usr/local/bin/m9m

curl -LO https://github.com/maharsolution/m9m/releases/latest/download/m9m-darwin-arm64
chmod +x m9m-darwin-arm64
sudo mv m9m-darwin-arm64 /usr/local/bin/m9m

Invoke-WebRequest `
-Uri https://github.com/maharsolution/m9m/releases/latest/download/m9m-windows-amd64.exe `
-OutFile m9m.exe

Each release ships SHA-256 checksums next to the binary — verify before installing in production.

docs.title: Verify installation
docs.text:
m9m version
m9m serve

# In another terminal
curl http://localhost:8080/health

docs.title: Data directories
docs.text:
m9m stores state under ~/.m9m/ by default:

Platform Location Linux ~/.m9m/ macOS ~/.m9m/ Windows %USERPROFILE%\.m9m\

Layout:

~/.m9m/
├── data/
│   ├── m9m.db        # Workflow storage (SQLite)
│   └── queue.db      # Job queue (SQLite)
├── config/
│   └── config.yaml   # Configuration
└── logs/
    └── m9m.log       # Logs

Override with M9M_DATA_DIR, M9M_CONFIG_DIR, M9M_LOG_DIR — see Environment Variables.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Fix command not found: m9m after Go install Add $(go env GOPATH)/bin to your $PATH. Postinstall download fails behind proxy (npm / pip) Set M9M_DOWNLOAD_BINARY=0 and stage ~/.m9m/bin/m9m manually. Docker container exits immediately Check that port 8080 isn't already bound: lsof -i :8080. Permission denied on Linux binary chmod +x the binary; verify it's not on a noexec mount. Homebrew tap not found Confirm the tap with brew tap and re-run brew tap neul-labs/tap.

docs.title: n8n ↔ m9m sync bridge
docs.text:
When you run the bundled docker-compose.yml, an HTTP service called sync-service runs alongside m9m-backend (managed by supervisord inside the m9m-backend container). It periodically polls n8n for active workflow and credential changes and pushes them into m9m via the public REST API.

The bridge is idempotent: re-running a cycle is safe. It is credential-aware: it decrypts n8n's AES-256-CBC + EVP_BytesToKey envelopes locally and re-encrypts them with m9m's at-rest key before pushing.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text: Scenario Use the bridge? Migrating from n8n to m9m, want to move workflows one by one Yes — let it poll and review before activating each in m9m Running n8n and m9m side-by-side, want a hot standby Yes — set SYNC_ONLY_ACTIVE=true and POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS=30 Greenfield m9m install, no n8n to pull from No — disable the sync service in docker-compose.yml One-off import of an exported workflow JSON No — use m9m exec workflow.json

docs.title: How it ships
docs.text:
The bridge runs inside the m9m-backend container, started by supervisord alongside m9m serve itself. The relevant docker-compose.yml block looks like:

services:
m9m-backend:
# ...
environment:
N8N_BASE_URL:            "http://n8n-designer-frontend:5678"
N8N_API_KEY:             "${N8N_API_KEY:-}"
M9M_BASE_URL:            "http://localhost:8080"
POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS:   "30"
SYNC_ONLY_ACTIVE:        "true"
SYNC_PORT:               "8001"
N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY:      "${N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY:-}"
N8N_PG_HOST:             "postgres-db"
N8N_PG_PORT:             "5432"
N8N_PG_USER:             "database_admin"
N8N_PG_PASSWORD:         "${N8N_PG_PASSWORD:-Secure_Db_Pass_2026}"
N8N_PG_DATABASE:         "n8n_prod"

The bridge listens on port 8001 by default; change SYNC_PORT to move it.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text: The bridge is a small FastAPI app exposed on port 8001 (or SYNC_PORT).

docs.title: GET /
docs.text:
Plain-text banner with the current config and a list of endpoints.

m9m <-> n8n sync bridge
  n8n:        http://n8n-designer-frontend:5678
  m9m:        http://m9m-backend:8080
  poll:       30s (background asyncio task)
  only_active: True
  sync port:  8001
Endpoints:
  GET  /        -> this message
  GET  /health  -> liveness probe
  GET  /status  -> last-cycle summary
  POST /sync    -> run one sync cycle now

docs.title: GET /health
docs.text: { "status": "ok" }

docs.title: GET /status
docs.text:
Last-cycle summary. Useful for health checks and dashboards.

{
"last_cycle_at":     "2026-09-11T08:30:00Z",
"last_cycle_source": "poll",
"last_cycle_count":  7,
"is_running":        false
}
Field Meaning last_cycle_at ISO 8601 timestamp of when the last cycle finished, or null if none yet last_cycle_source "poll" (background) or "manual" (triggered by POST /sync) last_cycle_count Number of workflows touched in the last cycle is_running true if a cycle is currently in progress

docs.title: POST /sync
docs.text:
Run one sync cycle synchronously and return the summary.

curl -X POST http://localhost:8001/sync

Response (HTTP 200):

{
"results": [
{ "workflowId": "wf-001", "name": "Daily Report",  "status": "ok"    },
{ "workflowId": "wf-002", "name": "Hourly Sync",   "status": "ok"    },
{ "workflowId": "wf-003", "name": "Webhook Echo",  "status": "failed", "error": "..." }
],
"started_at": "2026-09-11T08:30:00Z",
"duration_ms": 1423
}

If any result is failed, the response is HTTP 502 with the same body. The bridge does not raise on per-workflow failure — a single bad workflow does not block the cycle.

docs.title: Background polling
docs.text:
A background asyncio task polls n8n every POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS seconds (default 30) and pushes any changes into m9m. On startup, the task is created; on shutdown, it is cancelled cleanly. No external cron is required.

For each n8n workflow, the bridge:

  1. Fetches the full workflow from GET {N8N_BASE_URL}/api/v1/workflows/{id}.
  2. Computes a content hash and skips the workflow if it matches the last cycle's hash (no-op detection).
  3. Translates typeVersion (n8n's float) to an integer (m9m expects int) — lossy but adequate for parity.
  4. Pushes to m9m with POST /api/v1/workflows. On non-2xx that looks like a duplicate, retries with PUT /api/v1/workflows/{id}. Both failing logs the error and moves on.
  5. Pushes credentials it can decrypt from N8N_PG_* (see below); credentials whose data column is unreadable are skipped with a warning.

The bridge only runs against an instance it can reach over HTTP. If either n8n or m9m is unreachable, the cycle logs the error and waits for the next tick.

docs.title: Credential decryption
docs.text:
n8n's public REST API does not return the data field of credentials (it's marked writeOnly, and ?includeData=true returns redacted placeholders). To recover the actual encrypted blobs, the bridge connects directly to n8n's Postgres database and reads the credentials_entity.data column.

The data column is a JSON-encoded string of AES-256-CBC ciphertext with a random 8-byte salt prefix ("Salted__" + 8-byte salt + ciphertext), all base64-encoded. Decryption uses OpenSSL's EVP_BytesToKey MD5-based KDF — the same algorithm n8n uses (n8n/packages/core/src/Cipher.ts).

def decrypt_n8n_credential_data(ciphertext_b64, password):
raw       = base64.b64decode(ciphertext_b64)
assert raw.startswith(b"Salted__")
salt      = raw[8:16]
ciphertext = raw[16:]
key, iv   = evp_bytes_to_key(password.encode(), salt)
plaintext = AES.new(key, AES.MODE_CBC, iv).decrypt(ciphertext)
return json.loads(unpad(plaintext, 128))

password is the same key you set as N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY (or GEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY — both are accepted).

After decrypting, the bridge re-encrypts the plaintext credentials under m9m's at-rest key by POSTing/PUT-ing them through m9m's /api/v1/credentials endpoint. The plaintext is held in process memory only during the cycle.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Variable Required? Default Description N8N_BASE_URL yes http://n8n-designer-frontend:5678 n8n REST API base URL N8N_API_KEY yes — n8n API key (Settings → API in the n8n UI) M9M_BASE_URL yes http://m9m-backend:8080 m9m REST API base URL POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS no 30 Background poll cadence SYNC_ONLY_ACTIVE no true If true, only push active: true workflows from n8n SYNC_PORT no 8001 Port the bridge's HTTP API listens on N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY yes (for credentials) — The key n8n was started with; reads GEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY as fallback N8N_PG_HOST yes (for credentials) postgres-db Hostname of n8n's Postgres N8N_PG_PORT no 5432 Postgres port N8N_PG_USER no database_admin Postgres user N8N_PG_PASSWORD no Secure_Db_Pass_2026 Postgres password (change in production) N8N_PG_DATABASE no n8n_prod Postgres database

docs.title: Disabling the bridge
docs.text: If you do not want the bridge running, comment out the relevant block in docker-compose.yml (or set POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS=0 to make it a no-op — though the FastAPI process still listens on 8001, so the cleaner option is to remove the command: that runs supervisord and instead run m9m serve directly).

docs.title: Nodes Overview
docs.text: Nodes are the building blocks of m9m workflows. Each node performs a specific operation on data.

docs.title: Available Node Categories
docs.text:
Category Nodes Description Core 6 Workflow control, sub-workflows, no-ops Transform 9 Data transformation, conditionals, loops HTTP 1 Web requests Triggers 5 Workflow, error, and sub-workflow triggers Database 8 SQL, NoSQL, search, cache Messaging 4 Slack, Discord, Twilio, Microsoft Teams AI & LLM 2 OpenAI, Anthropic (also powers the in-app AI) Code 1 Python execution CLI Execution 1 Sandboxed CLI commands & AI agents Cloud Storage 4 AWS, Azure, GCP Productivity 3 Google Sheets, Notion, Stripe Version Control 2 GitHub, GitLab Email 2 SMTP, SendGrid File Operations 2 Read/write binary files Total 42

Numbers reflect the executor count returned by m9m node list (sourced from cmd/m9m/commands/exec.go::RegisterAllNodes).

docs.title: Node Structure
docs.text:
Every node follows this JSON structure:

{
"id": "unique-identifier",
"name": "Display Name",
"type": "n8n-nodes-base.nodeType",
"position": [x, y],
"parameters": {
"param1": "value1",
"param2": "={{ $json.dynamicValue }}"
},
"disabled": false
}

docs.title: Required Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description id string Unique identifier within workflow name string Display name (used in connections) type string Node type identifier position [x, y] Position in visual editor parameters object Node-specific configuration

docs.title: Optional Fields
docs.text: Field Type Default Description disabled boolean false Skip this node during execution

docs.title: Node Types
docs.text:
All m9m nodes use the n8n-nodes-base.* prefix for n8n compatibility:

n8n-nodes-base.start
n8n-nodes-base.httpRequest
n8n-nodes-base.set
n8n-nodes-base.filter
...

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text:
Nodes receive input data as an array of items and produce output data:

Input: [{json: {...}}, {json: {...}}]
           │
           ▼
    ┌─────────────┐
    │    Node     │
    │  (process)  │
    └─────────────┘
           │
           ▼
Output: [{json: {...}}]

docs.title: Input Data
docs.text:
• Nodes receive all items from connected upstream nodes
  • Each item has a json property with the data
  • Items may also have binary data for files

docs.title: Output Data
docs.text:
• Nodes can output zero, one, or many items
  • Output items are passed to all connected downstream nodes

docs.title: Expression Support
docs.text:
Most node parameters support expressions:

{
"parameters": {
"url": "https://api.example.com/users/{{ $json.userId }}",
"body": "={{ JSON.stringify($json) }}"
}
}

See Expressions for full documentation.

docs.title: Credential Injection
docs.text:
Nodes that require authentication can reference credentials:

{
"type": "n8n-nodes-base.slack",
"parameters": {
"token": "={{ $credentials.slackApi.token }}"
}
}

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
By default, node errors stop workflow execution. Use the Filter node to handle errors gracefully:

{
"type": "n8n-nodes-base.filter",
"parameters": {
"conditions": [
{
"leftValue": "={{ $json.error }}",
"operator": "notExists"
}
]
}
}

docs.title: In-app AI assistant (Settings → AI)
docs.text:
The AI assistant is a separate, in-app surface from the OpenAI / Anthropic workflow nodes. It powers "Ask AI to fix this", "Suggest next node", and the chat panel inside the workflow editor.

The assistant's provider, model, API key, and base URL are all configurable from Settings → AI in the web UI. The configuration is layered:

  1. Env defaults — M9M_AI_* (or legacy M9M_COPILOT_*) read at boot.
  2. DB-stored override — what you save in Settings; persists across restarts.
  3. Live UI toggle — the on/off switch in Settings.

The Settings value wins over env. Env wins over zero. See api/ai.md for the underlying /api/v1/ai endpoints.

docs.title: Supported providers
docs.text:
Provider Default baseURL Default models OpenAI https://api.openai.com/v1 gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini, gpt-4-turbo, gpt-3.5-turbo Anthropic https://api.anthropic.com claude-3-5-sonnet-latest, claude-3-5-haiku-latest, claude-3-opus-20240229 MiniMax https://api.minimax.chat/v1 MiniMax-Plus, MiniMax-Pro, MiniMax Ollama (local) http://localhost:11434/v1 Anything your local Ollama has pulled

Override baseURL if you run an OpenAI-compatible gateway, a self-hosted Anthropic proxy, or a regional Anthropic endpoint.

docs.title: MiniMax
docs.text:
MiniMax exposes an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint. m9m detects a MiniMax base URL by lowercased substring (minimax.chat or minimax.) and routes the call accordingly, so the assistant and the Anthropic workflow node can talk to MiniMax without code changes.

Configuration:

Env var Purpose M9M_AI_PROVIDER=minimax Selects the MiniMax provider preset M9M_AI_BASE_URL=https://api.minimax.chat/v1 Override the default M9M_AI_API_KEY=... MiniMax API key M9M_AI_MODEL=MiniMax-Plus Model name from MiniMax's catalog

Or in Settings → AI: choose the MiniMax provider preset, paste the key, pick a model.

docs.title: Curl — read effective config
docs.text: curl http://localhost:8080/api/v1/ai

docs.title: Curl — update config
docs.text:
curl -X PUT http://localhost:8080/api/v1/ai \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{
    "provider": "minimax",
    "apiKey":  "sk-...",
    "model":   "MiniMax-Plus",
    "baseUrl": "https://api.minimax.chat/v1",
    "enabled": true
  }'

docs.title: Curl — test chat
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/ai/test \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{"message": "Reply with the word OK."}'

Legacy M9M_COPILOT_* env vars (M9M_COPILOT_PROVIDER, M9M_COPILOT_API_KEY, etc.) remain honoured as aliases of M9M_AI_* so existing deployments continue to work. They will be removed in a future major release.

docs.title: CLI Nodes
docs.text: CLI nodes enable secure execution of command-line tools within workflows. The primary use case is running CLI-based AI agents like OpenAI Codex CLI, Claude Code, Aider, and similar tools in a sandboxed environment.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Modern AI coding assistants increasingly ship as CLI tools that can: - Analyze and modify codebases - Generate code from natural language - Debug and fix issues - Run automated refactoring

m9m's CLI Execute node allows you to orchestrate these tools within workflows while maintaining security through Linux sandboxing.

docs.title: CLI Execute Node
docs.text: Execute any CLI command with configurable sandboxing, isolation, and resource limits.

docs.title: Type
docs.text: n8n-nodes-base.cliExecute

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description command string Yes - The command to execute args array No [] Command arguments env object No {} Environment variables (key-value pairs) workDir string No - Working directory for execution shell boolean No false Run command through shell sandboxEnabled boolean No true Enable sandbox isolation isolationLevel string No standard Isolation level networkAccess string No host Network access mode timeout number No 60 Timeout in seconds maxMemoryMB number No 512 Max memory in MB inputFromPrevious boolean No false Send input data to stdin outputFormat string No text Output format additionalMounts array No [] Additional filesystem mounts

docs.title: Supported Agents
docs.text:
The CLI Execute node works with any CLI-based AI agent:

Agent Command Description Claude Code claude Anthropic's CLI coding assistant OpenAI Codex CLI codex OpenAI's code generation CLI Aider aider AI pair programming in terminal GitHub Copilot CLI gh copilot GitHub's CLI assistant Continue continue Open-source AI code assistant Cursor CLI cursor Cursor editor's CLI mode

docs.title: Example - Claude Code
docs.text:
Run Claude Code to analyze a codebase:

{
"name": "Analyze with Claude Code",
"type": "n8n-nodes-base.cliExecute",
"parameters": {
"command": "claude",
"args": [
"--print",
"--prompt", "Analyze this codebase and identify potential security vulnerabilities"
],
"sandboxEnabled": true,
"isolationLevel": "strict",
"networkAccess": "host",
"timeout": 300,
"maxMemoryMB": 2048,
"additionalMounts": [
{
"source": "/home/user/myproject",
"destination": "/workspace",
"readWrite": false
}
],
"env": {
"ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": "={{ $credentials.anthropicApi.apiKey }}"
}
}
}

docs.title: Isolation Levels
docs.text: Level Description Use Case none No isolation Development/debugging only minimal Basic filesystem isolation Trusted tools standard + PID namespace, resource limits Recommended for most agents strict + Network isolation, seccomp filtering Untrusted code analysis paranoid + No host filesystem access Maximum security

docs.title: Network Access Modes
docs.text: Mode Description When to Use host Full network access AI agents that need API access isolated No network Offline analysis tools loopback Localhost only Local services only

docs.title: Output Formats
docs.text: Format Description text Raw text output (default) json Parse stdout as JSON object lines Split stdout into array of lines

docs.title: Additional Mounts
docs.text:
Mount host directories into the sandbox:

{
"additionalMounts": [
{
"source": "/home/user/project",
"destination": "/workspace",
"readWrite": true
},
{
"source": "/home/user/.config/claude",
"destination": "/home/sandbox/.config/claude",
"readWrite": false
}
]
}

docs.title: Output Structure
docs.text:
Every execution returns:

{
"json": {
"exitCode": 0,
"stdout": "...",
"stderr": "...",
"killed": false,
"killReason": "",
"duration": 1500,
"cpuTime": 1200,
"maxMemory": 104857600
}
}
Field Type Description exitCode number Process exit code (0 = success) stdout string/object/array Command output (format depends on outputFormat) stderr string Error output killed boolean Whether process was terminated killReason string Reason if killed (timeout, signal, etc.) duration number Wall-clock time in milliseconds cpuTime number CPU time used in milliseconds maxMemory number Peak memory usage in bytes

docs.title: Sandbox Technology
docs.text:
On Linux, m9m uses bubblewrap (bwrap) for sandboxing:

  • Namespace isolation: PID, network, mount, user namespaces
  • Resource limits: cgroups v2 for memory, CPU, process count
  • Syscall filtering: Seccomp BPF for blocking dangerous operations
  • Filesystem isolation: Controlled mounts with read-only defaults

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
# Ubuntu/Debian
sudo apt install bubblewrap

# Fedora/RHEL
sudo dnf install bubblewrap

# Arch Linux
sudo pacman -S bubblewrap

docs.title: Default Security Settings
docs.text: Setting Default Memory limit 512 MB Timeout 60 seconds Max processes 50 Network Host (configurable) Filesystem Read-only mounts

docs.title: Blocked Syscalls (strict/paranoid)
docs.text:
• reboot, kexec_load - System control
  • mount, umount - Filesystem manipulation
  • pivot_root, chroot - Container escape
  • init_module, delete_module - Kernel modules
  • ptrace - Process debugging
  • setns - Namespace escape

docs.title: For AI Agents
docs.text:
1. Use appropriate isolation: standard for most agents, strict for untrusted code
  2. Set reasonable timeouts: AI agents may take minutes; use 300-600 seconds
  3. Allocate sufficient memory: 1-2 GB for most AI agents
  4. Enable network access: Most agents need API access to work
  5. Mount code read-only when possible to prevent accidental modifications

docs.title: For Security
docs.text:
1. Never disable sandbox in production
  2. Use read-only mounts unless writes are required
  3. Limit network access when API calls aren't needed
  4. Set memory limits to prevent runaway processes
  5. Review agent output before applying changes to codebase

docs.title: For Reliability
docs.text:
1. Handle non-zero exit codes in your workflow
  2. Parse stderr for error messages
  3. Check killed flag to detect timeouts
  4. Use JSON output format for structured data

docs.title: Agent not found
docs.text:
{"exitCode": 127, "stderr": "command not found: claude"}

Solution: Ensure the agent CLI is installed and in PATH, or use absolute path.

docs.title: Permission denied
docs.text:
{"exitCode": 1, "stderr": "Permission denied"}

Solution: Check mount permissions or use readWrite: true for mounts that need write access.

docs.title: Timeout exceeded
docs.text:
{"killed": true, "killReason": "timeout"}

Solution: Increase timeout parameter for long-running operations.

docs.title: Out of memory
docs.text:
{"killed": true, "killReason": "signal 9"}

Solution: Increase maxMemoryMB parameter.

docs.title: Quick Reference
docs.text: Parameter Recommended for AI Agents isolationLevel standard or strict networkAccess host (for API access) timeout 300 - 600 seconds maxMemoryMB 1024 - 2048 MB outputFormat json (for structured output)

docs.title: Code Nodes
docs.text: Code nodes execute scripts inside sandboxed runtimes. Unlike the Function node (which runs JavaScript), the Code category covers languages that need their own runtime.

docs.title: PythonCode Node
docs.text: Execute Python inside a bubblewrap-isolated environment. Use this for data wrangling, statistics, ML inference, or any task where JavaScript is a poor fit.

docs.title: Type
docs.text: n8n-nodes-base.pythonCode

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
• Code runs in a subprocess inside bubblewrap (bwrap) with no network and a writable /tmp only.
  • The Python interpreter is bundled with the binary (no host Python required).
  • Receives a data argument: a list of items (each { json: {...}, binary?: {...} }).
  • Must return a list of items. Returning an empty list halts the workflow downstream.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description code string Yes — Python source pythonVersion string No 3.11 3.10, 3.11, 3.12 timeout integer No 30 Max execution time, seconds memoryLimitMb integer No 256 Memory cap

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
"type": "n8n-nodes-base.pythonCode",
"parameters": {
"code": "import statistics\namounts = [item['json']['amount'] for item in data]\nreturn [{ 'json': {\n    'count': len(amounts),\n    'mean': statistics.mean(amounts),\n    'stdev': statistics.stdev(amounts) if len(amounts) > 1 else 0\n} }]",
"pythonVersion": "3.11",
"timeout": 10
}
}

docs.title: Stdlib and packages
docs.text:
• The full Python standard library is available.
  • A curated set of common third-party packages is pre-installed (numpy, pandas, requests, etc.).
  • For new packages, file an issue; pre-baked wheels reduce cold-start vs pip-install-at-runtime.

docs.title: Security model
docs.text:
• Process runs with the m9m binary's UID/GID; bubblewrap restricts filesystem visibility to a temporary scratch directory.
  • Network is disabled by default. Set network: true if the script needs to call out (rare; prefer an HTTP Request node).
  • Resource limits (memory, CPU time, wall-clock) are enforced by cgroups; over-quota scripts are killed and reported as errors.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Function node — JavaScript in-process, faster startup
  • CLI / Execute node — run arbitrary external commands (including AI agents) inside bubblewrap

docs.title: Core Nodes
docs.text: Core nodes provide fundamental workflow control functionality.

docs.title: Start Node
docs.text: The Start node is the entry point for workflows that don't use trigger nodes.

docs.title: Type
docs.text: n8n-nodes-base.start

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The Start node initiates workflow execution. It:

  • Passes through any input data provided
  • Creates an empty item if no input is given
  • Must be the first node in non-triggered workflows

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: The Start node has no configurable parameters.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
"id": "start-1",
"name": "Start",
"type": "n8n-nodes-base.start",
"position": [250, 300],
"parameters": {}
}

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
• None required - Creates empty item [{json: {}}]
  • Optional - Passes through provided input data

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
[
{
"json": {}
}
]

Or with input data:

[
{
"json": {
"inputField": "inputValue"
}
}
]

docs.title: Basic Workflow Entry
docs.text:
{
"nodes": [
{
"id": "start",
"name": "Start",
"type": "n8n-nodes-base.start",
"position": [250, 300],
"parameters": {}
},
{
"id": "next",
"name": "Next Step",
"type": "n8n-nodes-base.set",
"position": [450, 300],
"parameters": {
"assignments": [
{"name": "message", "value": "Workflow started!"}
]
}
}
],
"connections": {
"Start": {
"main": [[{"node": "Next Step", "type": "main", "index": 0}]]
}
}
}

docs.title: With Input Data (CLI)
docs.text:
m9m run workflow.json --input '{"name": "John"}'

The Start node passes through {"name": "John"} to connected nodes.

docs.title: With Input Data (API)
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/workflows/{id}/execute \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{"inputData": [{"json": {"name": "John"}}]}'

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text: Scenario Use Start Node? Manual execution Yes Webhook trigger No - use Webhook node Scheduled execution No - use Cron node Subworkflow Yes

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. One Start node per workflow - Only one entry point needed
  2. Position first - Place at the left of your workflow
  3. Clear naming - Keep the default "Start" name for clarity

docs.title: Related Nodes
docs.text:
• Webhook - HTTP trigger
  • Cron - Scheduled trigger

docs.title: NoOp Node
docs.text: The NoOp node passes its input through unchanged. It's useful as a placeholder, anchor point for connections, or visual divider while authoring a workflow.

docs.title: Type
docs.text: n8n-nodes-base.noOp

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
• Receives items from connected upstream nodes and emits them untouched.
  • Has no parameters, no credentials, and no side effects.
  • Common use: stub a node you intend to wire up later; mark a checkpoint; debug-flow anchor.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: None.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
"id": "noop-1",
"name": "Placeholder",
"type": "n8n-nodes-base.noOp",
"position": [450, 300],
"parameters": {}
}

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text: Scenario Use NoOp? Temporarily disable a branch Yes Anchor a sticky note visually Yes Stub a node you're about to wire up Yes Modify data No — use Set or Code

docs.title: Wait Node
docs.text: Pauses workflow execution for a fixed duration or until a specified date/time.

docs.title: Type
docs.text: n8n-nodes-base.wait

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Default Description resume string Yes time time (wait a duration) or specificTime (wait until ISO 8601) amount integer When resume=time 1 Amount to wait unit string When resume=time seconds seconds, minutes, hours, days dateTime string When resume=specificTime — ISO 8601 timestamp

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Wait 30 seconds:

{
"type": "n8n-nodes-base.wait",
"parameters": {
"resume": "time",
"amount": 30,
"unit": "seconds"
}
}

Wait until a specific datetime:

{
"type": "n8n-nodes-base.wait",
"parameters": {
"resume": "specificTime",
"dateTime": "2026-12-31T23:59:59Z"
}
}

docs.title: ExecuteWorkflow Node
docs.text: Calls another workflow by its id and feeds its output back into the current workflow.

docs.title: Type
docs.text: n8n-nodes-base.executeWorkflow

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
• Resolves the target workflow by stable id, not by display name, matching n8n's reference behaviour.
  • Accepts an optional workflowInputs mapping that injects JSON into the sub-workflow's $json.
  • Preserves the parent's EdgesTaken accumulator across the recursive invocation (see execution-edges).

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description workflowId string Yes Id of the workflow to invoke workflowInputs object No Map of field name → value injected into the sub-workflow's $json

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
"type": "n8n-nodes-base.executeWorkflow",
"parameters": {
"workflowId": "wf-abc-123",
"workflowInputs": {
"userId": "={{ $json.userId }}",
"feature": "report"
}
}
}

docs.title: Sub-workflow requirements
docs.text:
The target workflow must either:

  • Start with an executeWorkflowTrigger (recommended), or
  • Have a Start node that reads $json for the injected inputs.

docs.title: MySQL Node
docs.text: Run SQL queries against a MySQL / MariaDB server.

docs.title: Type
docs.text: n8n-nodes-base.mySql

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
• Supports the same operations as the PostgreSQL node (executeQuery, insert, update, delete).
  • Connection can be expressed as connectionUrl (e.g. root:pw@tcp(127.0.0.1:3306)/db) or as host/port/database/user/password.
  • TLS via the ssl parameter; off by default to match n8n's behaviour.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
"type": "n8n-nodes-base.mySql",
"parameters": {
"connectionUrl": "root:pw@tcp(127.0.0.1:3306)/app",
"operation": "executeQuery",
"query": "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?"
}
}

Postgres and MySQL default sslMode/ssl to disable to match n8n's behaviour against local databases. To enable TLS, pass sslmode=require in the connectionUrl or set the ssl flag explicitly.

docs.title: Retry on Failure
docs.text:
Use the Code node to implement retry logic:

const maxRetries = 3;
let attempt = 0;
while (attempt < maxRetries) {
try {
// HTTP request logic
break;
} catch (error) {
attempt++;
if (attempt >= maxRetries) throw error;
}
}

}
}

{"json": {"endpoint": "https://api.example.com/item/2"}}
]

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Use expressions for dynamic URLs - Build URLs from data
  2. Set appropriate headers - Include Content-Type for POST/PUT
  3. Handle errors - Check status codes with Filter node
  4. Rate limiting - Use Split In Batches for bulk requests
  5. Timeout handling - Set appropriate timeouts for slow APIs

docs.title: Operators
docs.text: Operator Description equals Equal to notEquals Not equal to contains String contains notContains String doesn't contain startsWith String starts with endsWith String ends with regex Matches regex pattern exists Field exists notExists Field doesn't exist greaterThan Greater than lessThan Less than greaterThanOrEqual Greater than or equal lessThanOrEqual Less than or equal between Between two values empty Is empty notEmpty Is not empty

docs.title: Code Node

docs.title: Type
